text: As Minister Gan Kim Yong has explained, ElderShield policyholders who decide not to join CareShield Life will remain covered by their existing ElderShield policy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I would also like to clarify that ElderShield Supplements will continue to be administered by the private insurers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: ElderShield Supplement policyholders will remain covered by their existing Supplement policy, regardless of whether they upgrade to CareShield Life or not.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In particular, there is a significant number of ElderShield 300 and uninsured individuals in the older existing cohorts who will have to pay a catch-up component to join and get onto CareShield Life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They may thus prefer to have the option to choose to join CareShield Life at their instance instead of being auto-enrolled and that is the thinking behind the scheme mechanism.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Nevertheless, I agree with Er Dr Lee Bee Wah’s point that it is important to reach out to these groups, too, to help them understand, to raise awareness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Certainly, we are of the view that if we design a scheme that is good and well, it is of no use if people do not understand it and do not know it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, I accept Er Dr Lee's point and I would also in return urge all Members of this House to use opportunities that you have on the ground in your events to explain the policy, to explain the scheme design and to reach out and explain and deal with queries that your residents may have.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Ms Irene Quay and Ms Anthea Ong have asked about the schemes available to help younger severely disabled Singaporeans, in fact, below the age of 30, including newborns, and whether it is possible to extend CareShield Life to these people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: CareShield Life is primarily designed to provide financial support for Singaporeans who become severely disabled during old age, which is when Singaporeans are most likely to need long-term care and support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Notwithstanding that, we have other schemes available which are outside the scope of the current Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But let me just outline some of them to help the younger severely disabled Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: First, MediShield Life will help to support their bills for inpatient and selected outpatient treatments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They can also benefit from other assistance schemes, such as the Assistive Technology Fund and the new Home Caregiving Grant, which I think Ms Anthea Ong mentioned, which does not have an age criterion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In addition, hospitals, such as KK Women’s and Children’s Hospital and the National University Hospital, offer programmes, such as subsidised therapy services, to help parents with children who need that specialised care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: On that score, I would like to assure Prof Fatimah Lateef that overseas Singaporeans can avail themselves of CareShield Life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They will be able to file CareShield Life claims from abroad wherever they may be, and to receive payouts to support their care costs in those chosen countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The second aspect of inclusiveness lies in making the claims process accessible and as seamless as possible, which several Members have raised queries and concerns about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Furthermore, the same assessment can then be made for other schemes as well, other different multiple schemes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In addition, policyholders need not pay for assessment fees for periodic disability reviews.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Such periodic reviews are, however, important to ensure that we continue to make payouts only to policyholders who are and remain severely disabled.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But to address Dr Lily Neo's concern, we will be adopting a more targeted approach for periodic disability reviews.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, the focus is on the ability or inability to do something.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In particular, we have been working with experts to improve the disability assessment framework, to explicitly recognise the impact of cognitive impairment on physical ability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is in line with requests from a number of Members for CareShield Life to also assist those who may have that mental condition or the cognitive impairment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: To elaborate on this, a policyholder may well be physically able to perform the various ADLs but require significant prompting or reminding as he is unable to remember what those steps might entail or how that is to be done.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Under the current framework, assessors who may not be sure how to assess this policyholder might well classify him as not being disabled, being able to perform the ADLs since he can physically complete them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Members have expressed concerns about vulnerable Singaporeans who may not be able to navigate the long-term care financing and social support landscape on their own.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Again, as I said earlier, we understand this and we want to ensure that Singaporeans know and understand the schemes well, that is, know how to make the claims, know when it applies to them and know what kind of claims to make.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: AIC, which administers all of MOH's disability schemes, and in particular the Silver Generation Office under AIC, will be our key partner in providing Singaporeans with guidance on the disability schemes they are eligible for, and also how to apply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At the same time, we will improve our coordination with the Social Service Offices and other Government touchpoints within the community, so that our support for vulnerable Singaporeans is more cohesive and also resides more closely to where the residents and the policyholders might be.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will also continually review our various initiatives to consolidate and, as far as possible, simplify them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We encourage Members to continue to refer needy individuals – and I think we heard some stories earlier – refer them to us, give us some specifics and we will reach out and see how we can assist.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Third, we recognise that not everyone can afford or will be covered by ElderShield or CareShield Life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Members have asked for more to be done to help such seniors who need financial support for their long-term care needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The CareShield Life and Long-Term Care Bill facilitates this by providing for cash withdrawals from MediSave for long-term care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: That is a more recent event and one which we believe strikes the right balance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Dr Lily Neo asked for more details on the eligibility criteria.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As Minister Gan Kim Yong has explained, this Scheme is targeted especially at Singaporeans who are unable to join CareShield Life, have low MediSave balances and also face financial difficulties in meeting their long-term care needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We recognise that individuals' circumstances from person to person may vary widely, and hence ElderFund is a discretionary scheme designed to take into account different circumstances as being applied to different persons.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Singaporeans who are unable to meet their long-term care needs even after relying on other sources of financing can be considered for ElderFund.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In response Dr Chia Shi-Lu's query on how we review ElderFund, we will review the adequacy of ElderFund payouts over time as we have more experience and we will also look at it in conjunction with several other factors that will determine the adequacy of the payout.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These new schemes and initiatives provided by this Bill should, however, not be seen in isolation, but instead, should be seen as complementary to the existing Government subsidies and assistance schemes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I have outlined a few, such as ComCare and MediFund, earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our system is designed to support all Singaporeans, regardless of their income levels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, it is that to which I now turn on the question of affordability, the second key principle behind the design architecture of the Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Affordability involves keeping CareShield Life premiums affordably priced, whilst at the same time also providing premium assistance to those Singaporeans who need it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: First, to ensure that CareShield Life premiums remain affordable, the ElderShield Review Committee had recommended that the CareShield Life Scheme focus on providing basic coverage for Singaporeans’ long-term care needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: One of their recommendations was to keep the existing ElderShield claim criteria, which is the inability to perform at least three out of six ADLs, a point that we have heard many Members touch on earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: That is anything in the order of 25% to 33% of increment, just by dropping down to two ADLs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The premium increase for CareShield Life would likely be significantly and also exponentially higher if the claims criteria are then further lowered to one ADL, given the higher incidence and length of disability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Not only will there be more persons with one or two ADLs, as opposed to three, but the period of support, which is for life, will also be for longer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Both will have an impact on the amount of premium that will have to be collected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Committee had also recommended that CareShield Life payouts start at $600 per month and increase over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Dr Lily Neo asked, and I think many others as well, such as Mr Chen Show Mao, if the payouts could be higher.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: CareShield Life payouts already start at an amount which is, at present, significantly higher than the current ElderShield scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Increasing the starting payouts from $600 to, say, $800 a month would also increase premiums for a 30-year-old policyholder by around a third.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, recall I said at the start that we have to find a design architecture for the Scheme that is affordable and that meets the interest of basic long-term care of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In addition, as Members would know, CareShield Life payouts are set to increase at 2% per year for the first five years of scheme implementation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Assuming a continued increase of 2% per year after that, that is 2% thereafter after the five years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, that is the projection that we take into account and also to keep up with the value of money over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, for those reasons, we have kept the focus on basic long-term care needs and looked at other ways to provide additional support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And I urge Members to remember that the payout from CareShield Life is intended and designed to be complementary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It complements the other pillars of financing support, not replace and not take over, and also not put in place and reduce others.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Lower- and middle-income Singaporeans, including those with moderate disabilities, will be supported with subsidies of up to 80% for residential and non-residential care services, and can also receive other disability grants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For example, the existing Pioneer Disability Assistance Scheme and the new Home Caregiving Grant, which will be launched at the end of this year, will provide support for persons with moderate disability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, the threshold will be different from what is otherwise required in the CareShield Life Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is less stringent than the severe disability claims criteria for CareShield Life and the current ElderShield, where a higher level of dependence is required for each ADL.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu and others in this House asked about the type of Supplements that will be offered by private insurers and whether MediSave can be used to purchase the Supplements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Singaporeans can purchase Supplements from the private insurers which currently provide coverage starting from two ADLs, and also a higher payout.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, you can choose either one or both of these Supplements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Dr Lily Neo asked if the Government could administer these Supplements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As I explained earlier, our approach for the Government in this Scheme is to provide basic coverage, whilst at the same time allowing the private sector to innovate in the provision of supplementary coverage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We believe that there are benefits to be reaped, for instance, in the diversity and type of products that are being offered, by allowing private insurers to compete in this space beyond the basic tier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Second, in response to Prof Fatimah Lateef's query, we keep premiums affordable by starting earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, that is one principle behind why 30 and not 40, which is ElderShield.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: A 30-year-old would have been working for some years at that age, and starting premium payment at that stage lengthens the payment duration and also reduces the annual premium payable, making CareShield Life premiums more affordable and more within reach, including for a person who has started work for some time at around 30.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Third, we allow the use of MediSave for CareShield Life premiums, similar to the approach for MediShield Life and ElderShield today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In response to Assoc Prof Walter Theseira's point, we allow the use of MediSave, but judiciously, because we recognise that it may be difficult for individuals to save and plan ahead for long-term care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We facilitate them starting these preparations early by allowing individuals to tap on their existing savings in MediSave as another financing source, instead of requiring them to use only cash which, as the Member knows, will cause a strain in their cashflow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This also helps to buffer individuals against the vagaries of life, sometimes from unintended or temporary unemployment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As a safeguard, we only allow MediSave to pay fully for basic healthcare and long-term care insurance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For additional coverage, we have set withdrawal limits to protect MediSave adequacy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is in line with the discipline that Assoc Prof Walter Theseira spoke about in the way in which we use MediSave to fund these schemes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Png Eng Huat also asked whether permitting MediSave uses for CareShield Life premiums would affect adequacy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The current MediSave contribution rates allow most working households in future cohorts and auto-enrolled existing cohorts to pay for CareShield Life, MediShield Life premiums and other healthcare needs from their monthly MediSave contributions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This includes permanent premium subsidies for lower- and middle-income policyholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Ms Jessica Tan, Miss Cheryl Chan and Dr Chia Shi-Lu asked some questions about this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In addition, we will also provide incentives to encourage existing cohorts to join the scheme, and these incentives are netted off against their premiums.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: While at Mr Leon Perera's point, I would like to clarify clause 15 of the Bill that allows the offsetting of premium subsidies from premium refunds, for administrative ease.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, let me just illustrate it with a scenario.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Any premium subsidies and incentives he received previously will then, of course, also be offset from this refund.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, you do not retain the subsidies whilst at the same time choosing to exit from the Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Separately, if the Council considers at its regular adjustments to consider premium rebates, for instance, in that situation, if there is a premium rebate to be paid to a policyholder, the rebate computation will not take into account the subsidy that has been given.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, if part of what you have been paying as a premium is assisted through the subsidy, then, the rebates that are given will not take that into account in giving the rebate to the policyholder.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Instead, the rebate will be retained in the fund, for the benefit of all the other policyholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Png Eng Huat also asked if the savings from Government administration have already been reflected in the CareShield Life premiums.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In any case, any further savings will be fully returned to policyholders, such as in the form of higher payouts or the premium adjustments that I just spoke about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In short, the Fund is not for profit and, should there be any surpluses, it will be put back into the Fund for the benefit of all policyholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Next, I would like to assure Members that no one will lose coverage due to his or her inability to pay.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But it has to be a genuine inability to pay, not just a refusal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu had a question about Additional Premium Support criteria for both CareShield Life and MediShield Life and whether we intend for it to be the same.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Members would agree that we must ensure that the long-term care financing system that we put in place must remain sustainable and must work in the long term.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is so that our children and the generations beyond that will not be unnecessarily and unduly burdened by the needs of the current generation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: First, CareShield Life and ElderShield are designed to be self-sustaining schemes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, that again is in the policy design.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This means that each cohort saves up for their own long-term care needs, and taps on these savings in their senior years, thereby minimising inter-generational transfers across cohorts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums are set based on this prefunding principle, and in line with internationally accepted industry standards and principles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Several Members – Ms Anthea Ong, Ms Irene Quay and Ms Tin Pei Ling – have asked about gender-differentiated premiums.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In particular, Ms Irene Quay expressed concern that gender-differentiated premiums could start the trend of potentially differentiating premiums in future by reference to other factors, such as race and so on.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have explained previously the actuarial basis for this feature, but we do recognise that there are other factors at play.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Actuarially, it is recognised that women live longer, are more likely to experience severe disability, and live longer in severe disability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In 2017, the average life expectancy at birth for women is 85.2 years, compared to 80.7 for men.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As individuals are more likely to become severely disabled in old age, women have a higher probability of becoming severely disabled in their lifetime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Three in five healthy women at age 65 are expected to become severely disabled, compared to two in five healthy men at age 65.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In addition, when disability happens, women are also likely to remain in disability for a longer period of time than men.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Women aged 60 are expected to spend 7.8 years requiring assistance with any of the ADLs, compared to 2.6 years for men.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And those are based on a study done in Singapore of Singaporean numbers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This means that women stand to receive more benefits from CareShield Life if you look at it across the spectrum and, hence, their actuarially priced premiums are higher.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We could average out the premiums across genders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But this only works if it was a fully universal scheme where there is no option.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As CareShield Life is optional for existing cohorts, gender-neutral premiums could well encourage male policyholders to stay on ElderShield and buy gender-differentiated Supplements from the private insurers, which may now then appear cheaper.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As Members know, the ElderShield premiums are gender-differentiated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Conversely, female policyholders would now find CareShield Life a much better deal than the existing gender-differentiated ElderShield.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This increases the risk of gender skewing in the risk pool as more women than men would join the CareShield Life Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The gender-neutral premiums would become increasingly unsustainable and premiums would have to increase, possibly approaching the level women would have had to pay anyway under a gender-differentiated scheme, but without covering a significant proportion of men.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In response specifically to Ms Irene Quay's query, I should explain that actuarial differences in claims experience by gender is well-established both locally as well as globally.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: However, there is limited data to support such differences based on other factors, such as race or genetic factors, which is why we look at this as an actuarial factor.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And ElderShield is supported by a series of other private insurers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Hence, the concerns I have just explained with regard to gender would not apply, and there is no impetus for us to differentiate CareShield Life premiums using these factors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Nonetheless, Members have raised fair concerns about affordability for women, and I think those are fair points, and the need for greater inclusiveness for a national scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, in absolute dollar terms, the Government subsidises women more, compared to the men in their age cohort and of the same income levels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I would also suggest to Members in this House that a gender-neutral premium, or gender-neutral scheme design, might, at first blush, appear inclusive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But if you take into account the factors that I have outlined, looking at that in terms of the payouts and the expected payouts and for the period of those payouts, then, in the longer term, it would likely lead to women from existing cohorts opting into CareShield Life, and men choosing to stay away.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We would then have a gender-skewed coverage, and this would have the unintended effect of further worsening national solidarity over the Scheme in the longer term.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu, Mr Png Eng Huat and Mr Leon Perera, amongst others, asked what information will be available about the administration of CareShield Life, the management of the insurance fund, and the premium pricing methodology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The public can be assured that the information shared will be similar to that for MediShield Life, and the CareShield Life Council will also consider what other information might be useful, having regard to industry norms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As we explained in Parliament in July last year when we debated the White Paper, premium pricing is an extremely complex exercise, and, in coming up with a scheme design, MOH has engaged professional actuarial consultants to construct an actuarial model to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For example, underlying assumptions include mortality and morbidity assumptions, and how these change over time and over age for the population.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Given these complexities, instead of just publishing a large number of actuarial tables, it is a lot more meaningful to release relevant information in a manner that can be easily understood and reviewed by a layperson.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I think Mr Png Eng Huat had a query on the US numbers; he had the 52% numbers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The query, I think, centred on the statistics that, in the US, 52% of the elderly would require long-term care assistance and asked whether this was taken into account.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This, along with information coming out from the UK and Japan, was not taken into account in computing the premium in this case.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: On the assumptions backing one in two that was shared previously – and I think that was the point Mr Png Eng Huat also raised – MOH had engaged the professional advice of actuaries to compute this estimate, using the assumptions, parameters and the model that I spoke about earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The projections are based on ElderShield claims experience but also draw information from a wider range of cross-sectional and longitudinal sources, given the limited experiences at older ages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As shared previously, the actuarial pricing data we look at includes insurance schemes in the US, Taiwan and South Korea.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It does not mean we used their data wholesale.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It looks at the models they have there, looks at our claims experience with ElderShield, draws them together, uses the models and gets the expertise of the actuaries and provides the scheme design.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Council could recommend for the surpluses to be returned in a number of ways, such as higher payouts over the years, reduced premium increases over the years, or premium rebates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We intend to give the Council the flexibility to study factors and to make recommendations so that they adequately respond to changing circumstances and the needs on the ground.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I should also outline that there is a publication by the Singapore Actuarial Society that is now available publicly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It provides a broad explanation of the key pricing assumptions and risks for long-term care insurance, the challenges for pricing long-term care insurance, the concept, the thinking behind the models and also, advantages of prefunding for long-term care insurance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: If Members are interested, this technical paper was recently released by the Singapore Actuarial Society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza asked about inter-generational equity, given that monies for both CareShield Life and ElderShield schemes will be placed in the same insurance fund.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For example, Government capital injections into the insurance fund, which are meant to support tail-end risks, can benefit the capital needs of both schemes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: However, monies maintained for CareShield Life and ElderShield will be tracked and accounted for separately.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As Minister Gan Kim Yong had explained earlier, one key role of the Council will be to make recommendations to the Ministry on the adjustments to CareShield Life premiums and payouts to ensure sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In response to Dr Chia Shi-Lu’s question on how often the premiums and payouts will be reviewed, let me assure Dr Chia Shi-Lu that the Council will monitor the disability trends and claims experience of the schemes closely and on a regular basis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Let them decide how regular they feel they need to, and it is possible that the review regularity may be more in the earlier years, as we start the administration of the scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will then determine the exact cycle for the adjustments thereafter, in consultation with the Council.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: To enable the Council to perform its functions, the Council will comprise individuals with different diverse backgrounds, ranging from healthcare practitioners, medical social workers, auditors, investment professionals, union members and also, an actuary who is a Fellow of the Singapore Actuarial Society, as Ms Irene Quay has suggested.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Council will also be supported by independent, external actuarial consultants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Third, again, similar to MediShield Life, the Bill also includes provisions for premium payment enforcement to enable us to take action against willful CareShield Life premium defaulters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: You have to be fair to all policyholders, and individuals do need to play their part by keeping up with and paying the CareShield Life premiums.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Enforcement provisions are, therefore, necessary to ensure that willful defaulters pay their premiums, instead of having their premiums unduly borne by other policyholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Fourth – and Mr de Souza raised this point – we intend to take a strong hand against fraudulent assessments and misuse of payouts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is commensurate with the more severe nature of these offences and also having regard to the fact that a nominated payee is acting on behalf of someone who is disabled.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: To Dr Chia Shi-Lu’s query on how we can further guard against fraudulent claims, let me assure Members that regular audits will be conducted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: No audit will be 100% foolproof, but audits will be done, patterns will be studied, to sieve out potential fraudulent claims.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, for instance, we might look at cases where a claimant who was assessed to be severely disabled and then subsequently assessed not to be not disabled at all, within a short period of time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These markers will allow my Ministry to look into further cases and investigate them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: To Miss Cheryl Chan’s query on whether we will audit nursing homes or service providers who have access to their patients’ payouts, let me first clarify that these providers generally only have access to the payouts if the policyholder or the caregiver had nominated these providers to receive the payouts on their behalf.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Where the policyholder lacks mental capacity to do so or/and is destitute, the nursing home can act on his behalf to apply for payouts, but this will be on very exceptional circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We would like to make clear that the audit and enforcement framework is not intended to penalise bona fide assessors or caregivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Sometimes, genuine bona fide mistakes are made and, sometimes, to answer Mr Christopher de Souza, for what might be a reasonable position.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: One could consider a situation where a caregiver living with a policyholder who uses part of the benefits for household expenses of the policyholder’s family when the policyholder's needs are already well taken care of.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, in other words, as part of the same household, needs are already taken care of, and the funds which are fungible are applied for another reason when the basic needs of the policyholder are already taken care of.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, in those situations, we do not intend to penalise the caregiver.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: To Mr Christopher de Souza's other query, it is, indeed, our intent to return payouts to policyholders in the event of misuse.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, those wrongfully received payouts will be put back into the Fund for the administrators to consider giving to the proper payee.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These monies can then be paid to that person or a nominated payee at the directions of the policyholder or the policyholder’s caregiver.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Like Ms Joan Pereira and Dr Chia Shi-Lu, we do take a serious view on data confidentiality and the safeguards in the Bill reflect this, as Minister Gan Kim Yong has elaborated upon earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Fifth, we must ensure that MediSave monies remain adequate to meet an individual’s healthcare needs in old age.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We all want to do a lot; we all want more payouts; we all want less premium, and we want there to be lower ADLs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: That, I think, is a summary of the debate that we had today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But remember what I said at the outset.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It must be designed for a broad majority of Singaporeans and kept affordable, and that has to be the design intent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I would also like to borrow Assoc Prof Walter Theseira's point so eloquently put, that we do have to use these schemes judiciously, we have to have an internal discipline to what can or cannot be used out of MediSave.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Members have raised several queries on the withdrawals from MediSave for long-term care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And some have also asked for the criteria to be relaxed so that we can extend the withdrawals to that of severely disabled children, parents or siblings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And yet others in this House have expressed concerns over the sufficiency of MediSave, given the increased flexibility.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is important to remember that MediSave's primary purpose is to help Singaporeans save up during their working years for their healthcare needs in their old age.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As a general broad proposition, I think that would find no quarrel.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Expansions or increases in MediSave usage will obviously impact adequacy for other healthcare needs, and they have to be considered carefully, as Assoc Prof Walter Theseira has outlined.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This ensures that the MediSave adequacy of the severely disabled member’s children and their ability to afford current and future healthcare expenses are not impacted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, that is also a cross-generation issue that Mr Christopher de Souza alluded to earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Singaporeans who are in financial need and have low MediSave balances may apply for other Government schemes, such as ElderFund, to obtain additional support for their long-term care costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is really about striking the right balance between the two competing interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Next, we have planned ahead with the Minister for Finance, setting aside the monies for the Long-Term Care Support Fund in advance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The majority of ElderFund beneficiaries are also expected to be in these cohorts, given the higher prevalence of disability in old age.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This Support Fund is sized to be more than adequate for these cohorts as they age into their silver years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, those are the parameters, and this is the cohort that we intend to look after with this Fund.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Nonetheless, as we progress and as there are more information and more claims experience, we will review the adequacy of the Long-Term Care Support Fund on a regular basis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: All three principles are essential for us to deliver a financing support system that can benefit all Singaporeans, regardless of income levels or disability status, for generations and, we hope, generations to come.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Members have asked about our communication and engagement efforts on the new schemes, and our efforts to explain the importance of planning ahead for long-term care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Since May 2018, we have, in fact, been busy engaging the public on these enhancements to our long-term care financing system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Ministry has held over 60 public briefings and engagement sessions to date and will continue to do more and spread information on this and educate the public, explain queries and help them with looking at their own landscape and deciding whether or not CareShield Life is suitable for them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is on top of the numerous briefings which I am sure all of us in this House would have diligently done at our grassroots events over the weekends and so on.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And I ask, as I did earlier, that this continue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As the Minister has mentioned earlier, CareShield Life will be launched around mid-2020 for Singaporeans born in or after 1980.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Given that these cohorts are younger, our engagement efforts for them will also have to be tailored to media platforms that are typically used by that generation of people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We aim to progressively launch CareShield Life for existing cohorts born in 1979 or earlier from mid-2021.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will commence engagement efforts for these cohorts closer to the launch in 2021.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Other than mass outreach in this fashion, the Silver Generation Ambassadors will also conduct face-to-face engagements with older Singaporeans in the existing cohorts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I hope this assures Members that the Ministry's efforts to ensure that Singaporeans from the existing cohorts are aware of the scheme’s benefits and will be able to make a considered decision on whether to join CareShield Life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Of course, in all of our engagement efforts, we will not just be explaining the features of CareShield Life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As Ms Tin Pei Ling pointed out, we will need to address the "why", and that is equally important.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have to explain why this is useful, and why planning for long-term care is important.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As Singaporeans live longer, our healthcare system has to evolve to better serve the needs of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have put in place measures to help Singaporeans remain healthy for as long as possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: On that, I thank Er Dr Lee Bee Wah for so warmly embracing HPB's efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We do believe that going upstream to ensure that we keep the healthy well for as long as possible should be the next bar.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At the same time, we will continue to invest in infrastructure and the services, as I outlined at the start of my speech, to support those who fall into disability.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: I am not going to make a long speech; do not worry.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Could I just ask a very simple question regarding the gender-differentiated premiums?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: The Senior Minister of State mentioned earlier that the concern is that if we do it as gender-neutral premiums, then we are going to be worried about men not wanting to come on the scheme.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: I am finding it a bit of a struggle to understand how do we know that that would be the case?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Maybe we should do a dip test here, but I just find that hard to understand.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They fall into disability and require support for a longer period of time.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, if you look at the scheme's design, if you fall into serious, severe disability, you will make the qualification and the payouts are then given.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Over time, that will have a bearing on the premium that will be payable.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We look at what insurance typically does, calculate it on the same basis.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But at the same time, outside of the scheme, we look at ways and means to assist.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And it is not just for the gender-differentiated premium.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We assist also those at the lower income.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is not built into the scheme's terms because that is not part of the actuarial calculations.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But at the same time, we use that which makes the integrity of the scheme actuarially correct.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But at the same time, using additional support mechanisms to support those and help those who may not be able to afford it.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, I hope that answers the Member's question.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But the Member may want to look at the paper that I can share with her that looks at this and looks at what impact this has on the way in which premiums are calculated.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: But while I agree with him that adverse selection is going to be a problem if you have gender-neutral premiums in the private market, I wonder what are his views on whether this would be an issue in the mandatory component of CareShield Life.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: Because with the mandatory component, the Ministry is, in fact, free to have gender-neutral premiums without incurring any sort of adverse selection there.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: I think the issue, really, is that although I generally believe prices must be right, there is an element of equity here and obviously many learned Members believe that it is important for there to be some kind of cost-sharing between the genders here.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: So, equity also is a consideration besides just prices being right here.

speaker: Deputy Speaker
text: We still have two more Bills after this.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Member's point concerns the impact that a universal scheme might have.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There is an option for the existing cohorts.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And that is where the differentiation will result in there being an imbalance.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: I would just like to ask him clarifications for the question I asked earlier, which is, if someone does not qualify because of the three ADLs, but with two ADLs or even one ADL, is somewhat unable to continue to work and earn an income and therefore has difficulties paying for the premium, is he or she still expected to continue to pay the premiums, in those kinds of situations?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: The second area – and I seek the Deputy Speaker's indulgence on this – I did not want to speak about the gender aspect because I had read the report, but after hearing the Senior Minister of State's round-up speech, I have to ask some questions.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: Just as it is an actuarial view of the risk factors, it is also a lens that we all put on to look at which risk factor or which differentiated factor we look at.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: Last night when I read the report again on the burden of disease, I actually looked at it from a gender differentiation lens.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: And therefore, I came to the same conclusion that, actuarially, it is a fair system to have that differentiation.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: But having heard this and hearing the point about the fact that this is a partial universal system and all that, if we took from an actuarial standpoint another factor, that is the risk factors affecting the disease burden or the disability, and I go back —

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Ms Tan, please do not make an advocacy for that point.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: On the point about the health factors that affect Singapore in 2017, it is really dietary risk, tobacco, high blood pressure and high blood sugar.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: A lot of these are due to lifestyle and also genetic factors.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: If we took that view and we put the same actuarial lens on it, then we would come to a different conclusion on the differentiation to be used for premium.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: I will ask the Senior Minister of State, with better experience, can we, at some point in time, with the experience of CashShield Life, as he has said it many times in his speech, can we relook, with that data, the experience and the trends, to see if premiums could be adjusted, at that point in time with better knowledge and intelligence from the data?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I think the short answer to the second question is certainly yes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But for now, I think the Member will remember that I have cited the paper which says that the period of time that a woman is living in disability is about three times – 2.6 and 7.8, I think it was.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And I think that is the type of number that actuaries would use to look at the calculations.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And particularly, as the Member Ms Jessica Tan has mentioned, if it arises from the one or two ADLs and he has lost his job, then I think a case can be made for support to be given to this policyholder.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Earlier on, there was a comparison about how high premiums could rise if we drop the qualifying criterion from three ADLs to two ADLs: that premiums will go up by one-third.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Is there a similar calculation the Ministry has done if indeed there were gender-neutral premiums?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: When you look at the way in which the current ElderShield policies are designed as well, that is no different.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I will make one other point, that when we look at the—the Member's earlier point was on the way in which we designed the Scheme?

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: The medical social worker will then be triggered.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: But for these families, since they put the seniors in nursing homes or since they need to hire a helper, what is the trigger point to let the agencies know that these families actually need additional help?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That is a broad question and I would say that we have a broad number of options available.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: When the Member said "trigger point", I am not sure I follow.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But obviously when a family is in need of assistance, there is a whole series of schemes that can be invoked.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I do not want to repeat them, but I have outlined them and the Minister has outlined them.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Member mentioned a helper; the Home Caregiving Grant does serve that need as well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And the criteria there is, of course, as I have mentioned earlier, the threshold is lower than the current CareShield Life ADL criteria.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, I hope that addresses at least a part of the Member's question.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If there is a specific point that the Member wishes to follow up on, I am happy to do so offline.      .
